newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kampo, Postal Savings suspend dealings with DKB.
newsitem.headline: Kampo, Postal Savings suspend dealings with DKB.

text.p: Japan's Postal Life Insurance System (Kampo) and Postal Savings System have suspended dealings with Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), a spokesman for the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said on Friday.

"Both Kampo and Postal Savings have suspended transactions with DKB until formal administrative punishment is taken. At that time we will again consider punitive measures against the bank," the spokesman said.
Both bodies use DKB for short-term fund management, purchasing certificates of deposit from the bank and making large term-deposits with it, he said.
On Thursday, Tokyo prosecutors arrested four DKB officials on suspicion of violating the Commercial Code.

The Prosecutors Office said in a statement that the DKB officials were suspected of giving loans worth 11.78 billion yen to Ryuichi Koike, a racketeer at the centre of a payoff scandal involving the nation's top brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
